# Invitation Maker

Invitation maker: wedding, birthday, baby shower and party invitations and greeting cards, generated with your details spelled out.

## What it does
Give the occasion, the main line, the details and a style. Claude tells you the price and creates the card.

**How the files are made:** each invitation is generated by an image model that MegaScenes runs through its model providers. Nothing is made until you say yes, and the price in credits comes first.

Image files in portrait; short, exact text works best.

## Install
In Claude Code:
```
/plugin marketplace add megascenes-app/claude-plugins
/plugin install invitation-maker@megascenes
```

## Connecting
- Invitation Maker talks to the MegaScenes server at `https://megascenes.com/api/claude/invitation/mcp` (Streamable HTTP).
- Connecting opens MegaScenes: sign in, create an account, or continue without one and add your email when you pay (OAuth with PKCE). Then you come straight back to the chat.
- Each invitation uses credits from your MegaScenes account and is priced before it runs; new accounts can start with a low-cost trial week.
- The invitations show in a viewer in the chat where Claude supports interactive apps; in Claude Code you get the links.

## Tools
| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `list_invitation_models` | Models for invitations with settings and starting prices. Read-only. |
| `estimate_invitation_cost` | Exact price of one invitation before it runs. Read-only. |
| `create_invitation` | Starts one invitation in your account. Uses credits; needs sign-in. |
| `get_invitation` | Status and file links. Read-only. |
| `get_account` | Your plan and credit balance. Read-only. |

## Example prompts
- "An elegant floral wedding invitation for Anna & Luca, June 12, Villa Rosa"
- "A playful 30th birthday party invitation"
- "A baby shower invitation in soft blue, Saturday at 3 pm"

## Data and privacy
What you give for the invitation (the occasion, the main line, the details and the style) goes to MegaScenes, stays in your MegaScenes account with the finished file, and is passed to the model provider that makes it. The plugin has no hooks or local scripts and sends nothing else.
